panels.title: Settled Transactions / min
panels.description: Core throughput indicator -- the closest proxy this demo has to 'revenue-generating activity per minute'.

panels.title: Failed Transactions / min
panels.description: Every failed transaction here is a candidate for real financial or reputational cost in a live trading platform -- retried settlement, counterparty friction, or a missed execution window.

panels.title: 30-Day Error Budget Remaining
panels.description: Directly implements the error-budget math from docs/SLO.md (99.5% target over a rolling 30 days). This is the number that should drive the 'pause feature work' conversation described in the SLO doc's error budget policy -- not a vague sense that 'things feel a bit broken lately'.

panels.title: Settlement Volume Trend (24h)
panels.description: Volume trend over the day -- useful for spotting whether a failure spike correlates with a traffic spike (capacity problem) or happened during otherwise-normal volume (a real regression).

panels.title: p95 Settlement Latency Trend (24h)
panels.description: Latency framed on a business timescale (24h trend, not a 5m incident window) -- the question this answers is 'is settlement getting slower over the day/week', not 'is something on fire right now'.

options.content: **Note:** this demo app has no real transaction-value data, so it does not compute an actual $ figure -- doing so here would be fabricated and misleading. In a real deployment, this panel would multiply the *Failed Transactions/min* metric above by an actual average transaction value (sourced from a real business metric, not guessed), to translate reliability directly into a number a non-technical stakeholder immediately understands. That translation -- engineering metric to business impact -- is the actual point of a business-facing dashboard, and it's called out explicitly here rather than faked with a made-up number.
